Package teilchen.constraint

Class Collider

java.lang.Object
teilchen.constraint.Collider
All Implemented Interfaces:
Constraint
Direct Known Subclasses:
LineCollider2D, PlaneCollider, SphereCollider, TriangleCollider, TriangleMeshCollider
public abstract class Collider extends Object implements Constraint
base class for colliders. colliders keep particles from passing through geometry ( planes, triangles, spheres, lines ).

colliders are constraints, i.e they are applied after integration. they test the path a particle traveled during the last step ( from old_position() to position() ) and therefore work with all integrators and do not miss fast particles ( no tunneling ).

on collision the particle is moved back to the free side of the geometry ( the penetration is mirrored and scaled by the coefficient of restitution ), the normal component of the velocity is reflected and scaled by the coefficient of restitution while the tangential component is kept. old_position() is updated accordingly so that colliders also work with Verlet integration.

  • Field Details

    • SKIN

      public float SKIN
      minimum distance particles are kept away from the surface after a collision. this prevents particles from resting exactly on a surface and being classified on the wrong side due to rounding.

    • MAX_ITERATIONS

      public int MAX_ITERATIONS
      maximum number of times a particle is resolved per step. more than one iteration is needed if resolving one contact causes another one, e.g in concave corners of a mesh.

    • pathStart

      protected final processing.core.PVector pathStart(Particle pParticle)
      Returns:
      start of the path the particle traveled during the current step. use this instead of old_position() for collision tests.

    • applyAll

      public static void applyAll(Physics pParticleSystem, List<Collider> pColliders)
      applies several colliders jointly. for each particle the earliest contact along its path ( over all colliders ) is resolved first, then the colliders are tested again. this is more robust than applying colliders one after the other, e.g for separate triangles that form a connected surface. Physics uses this for all colliders in its constraints.

    • resolve

      protected final void resolve(Particle pParticle, float nX, float nY, float nZ, float pPenetration)
      resolves a collision. the contact point is the projection of the particle onto the surface.
      Parameters:
      pParticle - colliding particle
      nX - x component of the unit contact normal ( pointing to the free side )
      nY - y component of the unit contact normal
      nZ - z component of the unit contact normal
      pPenetration - distance the particle must move along the normal to reach the surface ( > 0 )

    • resolve

      protected final void resolve(Particle pParticle, float nX, float nY, float nZ, float pPenetration, float cX, float cY, float cZ)
      resolves a collision.
      Parameters:
      pParticle - colliding particle
      nX - x component of the unit contact normal ( pointing to the free side )
      nY - y component of the unit contact normal
      nZ - z component of the unit contact normal
      pPenetration - distance the particle must move along the normal to reach the surface ( > 0 )
      cX - x component of the point where the path of the particle reached the surface
      cY - y component of contact point
      cZ - z component of contact point

    • owner

      public void owner(Force pOwner)
      links collider to a force ( e.g a deprecated *Deflector ). the collider is skipped if the force is inactive and becomes dead if the force is dead or was not applied in the current step ( i.e removed from the physics ).
